block.title: in-game pixel sprites: halo crystal, option hunter, glint mote
block.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art sprite sheet for a retro arcade shoot-'em-up, flat deep-navy background, bold dark navy outlines, saturated limited palette, dithered shading, no scene, no text, no labels, no UI. Arranged in three clean rows facing left: row one is the OPTION HUNTER in three scales — the full armored deep-violet frigate with wedge prow, four open magnetic grapple-claws on its flanks and a violet glowing belly launch bay, then a medium view where one claw is closed around a captured drone-orb, then a close-up of the launch bay mouth alone, violet light spilling out; row two is a HALO CRYSTAL shown through one full rotation in eight frames — a big faceted violet gem with lilac edge-glints and a ring of six smaller satellite crystals turning around it, the ring's position stepping smoothly frame by frame while the central gem keeps an identical silhouette; row three is the GLINT MOTE in five frames — a fist-sized crystal spark whose edge-lights strobe bright-lilac to dim and whose tiny satellite flecks orbit, plus one frame of the mote bursting into a harmless star-puff. Every sprite crisp, readable at game scale, consistent lighting from above.
